Mercer Frey: Snow Veil Sanctum. Gallus's tomb. Karliah's little stage for murder. I've not set foot here since the day I found his body. Serana: A crypt full of dead Nords and one vengeful ghost lover. Sounds like a typical Tuesday in Skyrim, really. At least the weather's agreeable—no blizzard to distract from the backstabbing. Lydia: I'd rather face a hundred Draugr than trust a thief who drags us into a necropolis without a plan. But if Karliah wants blood, she'll get steel. And if you try any tricks, Mercer, my blade will find your spine.

Serana: So this Karliah was sleeping with Gallus, then shot him through the throat and poisoned you for good measure. Nice. She sounds like my kind of woman—efficient, vengeful, and knows how to make an exit. Dibella would be proud of that dramatic flair. Lydia: A murderous Dunmer whore who betrayed her own Guild and lover. Sounds like typical elven treachery to me. At least when Nords kill someone, we look them in the eye and give them a chance to draw steel first. Mercer Frey: You weren't there, Lydia. You didn't see the way she moved—silent as shadow, cold as winter. Karliah didn't give Gallus a warrior's death. She gave him an assassin's. And now she's hiding in his tomb like a coward, defiling his memory with her presence.

Serana: Night falls, and someone found a Rueful Axe. Did you mug a daedra worshipper on the way here, or is that just standard Skyrim grave-robbing decor? Dibella would approve of the aesthetic—blood-red stains really bring out the snow. Lydia: That axe belonged to a fool who made a deal with a daedra. I'd rather trust my greatsword than some cursed relic promising vengeance.

I'll keep it as a reminder that elven treachery leaves a trail of silver and blood. Mercer Frey: Enough preening. Serana: Well, that was invigorating. Nothing like a surprise ambush to get the blood pumping—or in my case, the ancient vampire fluids circulating. Lydia, darling, did you enjoy your nap on the cold stone? Paralyzed so quickly. I thought Nords were supposed to be resilient. Lydia: A lucky spell from some half-rate mage.

Mercer Frey: These draugr are getting thicker than flies on a corpse. I've seen enough ancient Nord tombs to last three lifetimes, but this one has a particular stench to it. I've studied enough magic to know that particular spell doesn't come cheap or clean. Mercer Frey: A man picks up a few tricks along the way, Daegon. Call it an investment in personal security. But if you start glowing and craving raw meat, I'm setting you on fire. Mercer Frey: Noted. Now, that skeleton key is somewhere in these halls. Let's stop chatting and start looting.

Mercer Frey: Well, that was a proper bloodbath. More than I expected for a simple tomb raid. But the path ahead is clear now, and I can almost taste that key. Daegon: Simple. Right. Because ancient Nordic crypts filled with draugr, rogue mages, and hired thugs are always so straightforward. You Guild types have a strange definition of simple. Mercer Frey: You get used to it. The job's always the same - get in, grab the prize, get out. The bodies just change depending on who's stupid enough to stand in the way. Mercer Frey: The Skeleton Key belongs to the Guild. What I do with it after I hand it over to Karliah and the others... well, that's between me and my conscience. And we both know a thief's conscience is flexible. Daegon: Karliah. Now there's a name that stirs up stories. The Nightingale who vanished. I've heard whispers about her and Mercer Frey in the same breath more than once. Something about a betrayal, a murder, and a whole lot of bad blood. Mercer Frey: Whispers are cheap, Daegon. Everyone in Riften has a story about someone else. What matters is what's real, and what's real is that key opens a door I need opened. The rest is just noise. Daegon: For someone who claims not to care about stories, you sure are quick to shut down questions about that one. Makes a girl wonder what you're hiding under all that Guild Master charm.

Mercer Frey: More draugr. And skeevers too. This place just keeps giving. Focus on the key, not on old stories, Daegon. We're close now - I can feel it. Daegon: Keep your secrets, Guild Master. I'm more interested in getting out of this crypt alive anyway. Just try not to get yourself killed before you show us that famous lockpicking technique. Mercer Frey: Worry about your own skin, elf. I've been walking out of tombs like this since before you were born. Now let's clear these bones and find my prize.

Mercer Frey: These draugr are getting thicker than flies on a corpse. Makes me wonder what the Nightingales really know about this place that they didn't tell me. Darling, you're standing next to a woman who's been cold for centuries. Try being entombed in ice for a few thousand years, then complain about the temperature. Mercer Frey: That's Stefani taken care of. Shame she couldn't see reason. Serana: Another one who thought she could outrun fate. I've seen that look before - desperation mixed with a bad plan. Daegon: She was a fool to work with the Silver Hand. They never pay well enough for that kind of risk. Mercer Frey: Speaking of risks, we're getting closer to the inner sanctum. I can feel it. Mercer Frey: Damn traps! This place is tighter than Maven Black-Briar's purse strings. Watch your step. Daegon: That archway looks like something out of a nightmare. The Nords really knew how to set an atmosphere. Serana: At least the dart wasn't poisoned. I've had worse mornings waking up next to a hungry thrall. Lea' Saa has some nerve ambushing us here. Mercer Frey: She's working with the Silver Hand, which means she knows we're coming for the key. No more playing nice. Daegon: Playing nice went out the window when we stepped into this crypt. Mercer Frey: More bodies for the pile. That Nord woman had some fight in her, I'll give her that. But she was still just another obstacle. Serana: I counted three of them thinking they could take us with rusty axes and bad attitudes. Reminds me of my father's court - all brawn, no brains, and a short lifespan.

Mercer Frey: The Skeleton Key's close now. I can feel Nocturnal's influence thickening in the air like perfume on a whore. Daegon: Perfume or not, this place reeks of death and old magic. The kind that sticks to your bones. Serana: Old magic, new corpses. Same song, different verse. At least the entertainment's been decent so far. Mercer Frey: Keep your wits about you. The Sanctum's heart is just ahead, and whatever guards it won't be as easy as these hired blades.

Mercer Frey: Another one down. Mikaela fought like she had something to prove. Pity she chose the wrong side. Daegon: The wrong side, the wrong contract, the wrong tomb. Some people just can't read the signs.
